subject: Request for evidence: segregated no-training routing and subprocessor proof — MediaSpring pilot
messages:
From: Lydia Carter <lydia@mediaspring.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@mediaspring.io>
Date: 2026-11-24T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Request: segregated routing proof for no-training commitment

Hi Jonas,

As part of our procurement review for the MediaSpring pilot we need evidence that Redwood's 'no-training' commitment is operationally enforced for our tenant data. Specifically we need:

- a current subprocessor inventory (including any cloud partners and managed services)
- an architecture diagram showing how tenant requests are routed and segregated (SFTP vs API export lanes)
- sample logs or attestations showing no model updates from tenant interactions (or a description of telemetry retention windows)
- confirmation of KMS regions and whether keys are customer-dedicated

Attached is our DPA questionnaire (Mediaspring_DPA_questionnaire.pdf). Could you confirm whether you can provide SFTP export proofs vs API-delivered evidence and an ETA? We're on a procurement deadline the week of Dec 6.

Thanks,
Lydia

-- 
Lydia Carter
Head of Security & Compliance
MediaSpring
Attachment: Mediaspring_DPA_questionnaire.pdf (pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Carter <lydia@mediaspring.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: segregated routing proof for no-training commitment

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear list. We can provide an evidence pack but want to make sure we deliver what your legal/procurement team needs. Immediate plan: 

1) I can share our current subprocessor inventory and a sanitized architecture diagram.
2) We can produce a short extract showing telemetry retention windows and an explanatory note on model update safeguards (no-training enforcement).
3) For concrete artifacts we can either: provide SFTP-delivered export slices (redacted) or an API-delivered evidence bundle. Which do you prefer?

I've attached a prelim-evidence-checklist xlsx that maps your asks to what we can produce quickly. If you confirm SFTP vs API preference, we'll lock an ETA — aiming for 3 business days for a sanitized pack. If you need raw logs for in-house review, we'll need an extra security sign-off.

Attaching: prelim-evidence-checklist.xlsx

- Jonas

-- 
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: segregated routing proof for no-training commitment

Jonas — looping Security/Ops (David) is the right call. A couple of operational notes before we hand anything to MediaSpring: 

- We can provide a subprocessor CSV and a sanitized diagram, but we should redact internal cluster hostnames/IPs and any proprietary routing rules. See our redaction-guidelines.md for the team standard.
- Logs: prefer to provide aggregated attestations (e.g., token-level telemetry retention windows + a hashed sample) rather than raw logs. Raw logs require a data-sharing agreement and additional approvals.
- KMS: confirm whether MediaSpring wants to see region names only or a statement on whether keys are customer-dedicated vs Redwood-managed. We generally provide region + key management model; customer-dedicated keys are only for Dedicated/Private customers.

If David confirms, I can draft a sanitized evidence pack template and shepherd it through Legal for a brief addendum to the DPA.

Kimberly

Attachment: redaction-guidelines.md

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Carter <lydia@mediaspring.io>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@mediaspring.io>
Date: 2026-11-27T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: segregated routing proof for no-training commitment

Hi Lydia — quick update and delivery of initial evidence. Thanks for the patience. Per the checklist, here are the items we can deliver immediately and the next steps: 

1) Subprocessors: attached CSV (redwood_subprocessors_nov2026.csv) — includes cloud infra, CDN, audit-log processor. This is the current inventory; we can flag any third parties you want more detail on.

2) Segregated routing and proof: attached diagram (segregated_routing_diagram.png) shows tenant-routing lanes and the export paths (SFTP export queue vs API evidence bundle). The diagram is sanitized to remove internal hostnames per our redaction policy.

3) Telemetry/No-train attestation: Redwood does not use tenant interactions to continuously adapt public models for hosted customers under the standard DPA terms. We retain transient KV/prefix cache for session performance; persistent telemetry used for product improvement is scoped and governed by contracts. We've included an operations note in the evidence pack describing retention windows and how model-update pipelines are gated.

4) KMS and residency: Keys used for encryption-at-rest are Redwood-managed for hosted customers; KMS region information is noted in the CSV. If you require a customer-dedicated KMS (bring-your-own-key), that is available for Dedicated/Private deployments and would be covered under a separate addendum.

5) DPA addendum draft: attached (dpa_addendum_draft.docx) — this contains proposed language for a no-training clause and a short SFTP/API evidence delivery SLA.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_nov2026.csv, segregated_routing_diagram.png, dpa_addendum_draft.docx

Next steps: please confirm whether you want the evidence bundle delivered via SFTP (we can provision a temporary, read-only export for your security team) or as an API-delivered zip with signed checksums. If SFTP, confirm a contact and we'll schedule the transfer — target turnaround: 3 business days to produce the sanitized pack after confirmation.

If you want more granular logs for an audit team, we can discuss redaction and an NDA amendment.

Best,
David Kim
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
